title: Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19)
description: The Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19) dataset contains overnight home recordings from 20 subjects who each slept four nights with partial polysomnography (EEG, EOG, chin EMG), dry-contact ear-EEG, and a wrist-worn actigraph. Ten of these subjects also completed 12 further nights with only ear-EEG, actigraphy, and a single EOG electrode. The dataset also includes sleep scoring, post-night comfort questionnaires, sleep diaries, and electrode quality-check markers. It was collected to develop and assess ear-EEG as a sleep monitoring platform.
methods_description: Recordings were made in the subjects' own homes between 2018 and 2020 using a TMSI Mobita EEG recorder with dry-contact ear-EEG electrodes, along with GENEactiv actigraphs. Subjects filled in a questionnaire and a diary after each night. Each recording began with a shared shaking of the recorder and actigraph to allow alignment, followed by an electrode test video (jaw clenching, eye opening and closing, horizontal eye movements). The only EEG preprocessing was setting electrodes with faulty shielding to NaN in the .set files.
